yourTurn.question: Outline the mechanism of aerobic respiration.
solution: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm: glucose is broken into two pyruvic acid molecules, with two ATP and two NADH formed.
When oxygen is available, pyruvic acid moves to the mitochondrial matrix and is converted into acetyl coenzyme-A.
In the Krebs cycle, acetyl coenzyme-A is completely oxidized to carbon dioxide, forming ATP, NADH and FADH₂.
The electron transport chain occurs on the inner membranes of mitochondria; electron flow releases energy used to make ATP.
At the end of the chain, electrons and hydrogen ions combine with oxygen to form water.

explain.title: Cellular respiration releases energy

explain.title: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen
explain.body: Cellular respiration occurring in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration. It is the complete oxidation of glucose with maximum release of energy.

notes.title: ATP: the cell’s energy currency
notes.answer: ATP is a nucleotide that stores and transfers usable energy for cell activities.
notes.explanation: ATP is a nucleotide made of adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups. The bonds between its phosphate groups are high-energy bonds. When the outer phosphate bond breaks, ATP becomes ADP, inorganic phosphate (Pi) separates, and about 7.3 kcal of energy per mole is released. Cells use energy from food to join ADP and Pi and make ATP again. For example, ATP can break down to release energy for a cell process, while energy from food can be used to rebuild ATP.
notes.simple: ATP is like a small energy packet. Breaking off its outer phosphate releases energy, and cells can use energy from food to attach a phosphate again.
examples: ATP + H₂O → ADP + Pi + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)
ADP + H₂O → AMP + Pi + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)

Cells use energy from food to combine ADP and Pi and make ATP again.

notes.title: Photosynthesis
notes.answer: Photosynthesis is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight (and chlorophyll), with oxygen as a by-product.
notes.explanation: Photosynthesis is how plants, algae and some bacteria use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. It happens in two phases: light reactions in the thylakoid membranes and dark reactions in the stroma. Chlorophyll absorbs light, and the light reactions make ATP and NADPH for the dark reactions.
notes.simple: Plants use light to make food. The light reactions capture energy, and the dark reactions use that energy to make carbohydrates.
examples: Light reactions release oxygen when light breaks water molecules.
In the dark reactions, carbon dioxide is used to make carbohydrates.
steps: The light reactions use light energy to make ATP and NADPH and release oxygen from water.
The dark reactions use ATP and hydrogen from NADPH to reduce carbon dioxide and make carbohydrates.
The carbohydrates are used to make glucose.

notes.checkAnswer: Light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes; dark reactions occur in the stroma.

notes.title: Cellular Respiration
notes.answer: Cellular respiration is the oxidation of food inside cells to release energy.
notes.explanation: Cellular respiration releases energy by oxidizing food inside cells. With oxygen, glucose is completely oxidized and releases more energy; without oxygen, glucose is incompletely oxidized and releases less energy. The main stages of aerobic respiration are glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain.
notes.simple: Cells release energy from food. Oxygen allows more energy to be released; without enough oxygen, cells release less.
examples: In yeast, pyruvic acid is converted into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide.
In hard-working muscles when oxygen is insufficient, pyruvic acid is converted into lactic acid.
steps: In glycolysis, one glucose molecule is broken into two pyruvic acid molecules in the cytoplasm.
When oxygen is available, pyruvic acid is converted into acetyl coenzyme-A and enters the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix.
The Krebs cycle produces carbon dioxide, ATP, NADH and FADH₂.
In the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membranes, electrons release energy used to make ATP; oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.
notes.checkQuestion: Where does glycolysis occur, and does it need oxygen?
notes.checkAnswer: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen.

notes.title: Bioenergetics: energy in living things
notes.answer: Photosynthesis stores energy in glucose, and cellular respiration releases energy from glucose for cell activities.
notes.explanation: Cells need a steady supply of usable energy. In this chapter, ATP links the energy released by respiration to the work cells perform, while photosynthesis stores light energy in glucose.
notes.simple: Photosynthesis stores energy in glucose. Respiration releases energy from glucose, and ATP carries usable energy around the cell.
examples: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen.
Aerobic respiration: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy.
steps: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy during photosynthesis.
Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen.
Respiration breaks down glucose and transfers some of its energy to ATP.
With oxygen, aerobic respiration produces much more ATP than anaerobic respiration.
Without enough oxygen, cells can use anaerobic respiration, which produces less ATP.

notes.checkAnswer: ATP is the cell’s usable energy carrier; ADP can gain a phosphate group to become ATP.

written.text: Q8.1. Explain ATP as a molecule that is the chief energy currency of all cells.

written.text: Q8.5. Outline the mechanism of aerobic respiration.
modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen.
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and breaks glucose into pyruvate, producing a small amount of ATP and NADH.
Pyruvate enters the mitochondrion and is further broken down; the Krebs cycle releases carbon dioxide and transfers energy to carriers.
Electrons pass along the electron transport chain in the mitochondrion.
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and combines with hydrogen to form water.
Most ATP is produced during the electron transport chain.
